revision_summary: One quote-accuracy fix and two schema/tone corrections needed: (1) The observed_outcome quote at claimed ts 08:44 does not exist at that timestamp — it's a composite paraphrase of the rep's actual lines from 09:09-09:14 ('yeah. Sorry. It's cutting out pretty bad. So, but, yeah, I'll try calling some other time, though...'). Correct the ts to 09:09 and quote the transcript verbatim rather than compositing across turns. (2) In cherry_pick_moments[0], the schema_reference 'protocols (non_standard_scenario_hold — new category)' fabricates a protocol name not present in the schema's protocols section; relabel this as a proposed/TBD gap (similar to how the schema itself flags TBD protocol additions) rather than citing it as an existing or quasi-existing schema key. (3) Soften the accusatory tone around the 06:22 'manufactured excuse' read in both cherry_pick_moments and coaching_focus — the alternative_hypothesis is present and reasonable but the primary stewart_read and coaching language state the deception theory with more confidence than the ambiguous evidence (a possibly genuinely confused/rambling elderly caller) supports. Additionally, consider adding note that the customer's communication pattern throughout (short flat answers, rambling tangents, scam-call wariness at 07:04-07:08) suggests a possible elderly/vulnerability context per context.customer_demographics and coaching_philosophy.empathy_on_vulnerability_disclosure, which reframes the coaching lens from pure 'rep failed to control the call' to 'rep may have needed a patience-first approach with a distractible elderly customer.' These are targeted fixes; the core trajectory read (derailed call, DQ facts surfaced but not named, no-appointment outcome) is sound and well-grounded.
